D16·eyzp — 2026-09-21
rule: Every L-row fix cycle must name a loss-specific metric (a deterministic replay of the recorded loss where possible) as its primary score; hidden-test pass is only a non-regression guard for it.
chose: D13 AMENDED again (operator ruling, 2026-09-21): an L-row cycle is scored on the LOSS'S OWN SIGNATURE, not on hidden tests. For 3.4 the row is L11, with base 48f63b2^ and human comparator 48f63b2. PRIMARY: replay round 1's recorded failing phase-update calls (claude-sofar/r3 S7 and S8 invalid_input; claude-sofar/r1 S9's full-replace plan update that wiped phases 6–8) against each candidate build (loop, direct, human). Each replay starts from the cell's record truncated to just before the call. It is deterministic and costs $0, with no model. SECONDARY, as a non-regression guard only: hidden tests on S1–S9 at haiku, 1 rep per candidate. The evaluator adopts the bench-refresh weekly-reset cap (--week-reset, bench-refresh 01M31Q1F) before any launch.
over: Scoring an L-row cycle by hidden-test pass alone (D1's default metric), which cannot see a bookkeeping loss, so every verdict would be noise.
because: The hidden tests score the app the agent builds. A bookkeeping loss (a refused phase update, a wiped plan, a split session) barely moves that, and most of r1-fixes' L-rows are bookkeeping losses. A replay of the recorded failing calls says directly whether a build removes the loss. The hidden-test run stays only to catch a fix that breaks the agent's work.
